resources.string: Save a remote MCP server, test it from TermiNow, then add it to Claude Code in TermiNow or in your Ubuntu. Claude Code keeps using your own login.
Adding a local command server to Claude Code from TermiNow is not supported yet. Add it in Claude Code with claude mcp add NAME -- COMMAND ARGUMENTS.
Profile saved, but its credentials are missing. Edit it to enter them again
Written to %1$s, but Claude Code did not confirm it · %2$s
Disabled: removed from Claude Code, the profile is kept
The test checks the connection from this app only, not from Claude Code in the selected environment.

Allow plain HTTP to MCP servers on this device only (localhost and 127.0.0.1), like a server you run in a terminal while developing it. Everything sent over HTTP, including tokens, is unencrypted. Other servers always need HTTPS with a valid certificate.

Not in this release: OAuth sign-in from TermiNow, configuring SSH hosts, and adding local command servers to Claude Code. For OAuth servers, add them without credentials and sign in with /mcp in Claude Code.
Use letters, numbers, - and _ only, as Claude Code requires
Another MCP server has this name
Saved, leave empty to keep it
Add at least one header, or choose None
Tokens and header values are stored encrypted with a key in the Android keystore and are never shown again. OAuth sign-in is not supported in TermiNow in this release.
No Ubuntu is installed. TermiNow does not install one, use proot-distro in a terminal. SSH hosts are not supported yet.
Each environment has its own home and Claude Code configuration. SSH hosts are not supported yet.
Project directory, in the target environment
Enter the absolute path of the project directory
A shared .mcp.json is often committed to version control, so it can not hold credentials. Use the user or private project scope for this server.
Saved. Configure Claude Code again to use the changes there
Delete the MCP server %1$s from TermiNow?
Delete the MCP server %1$s from TermiNow? It is still in the Claude Code configuration, which this does not change. Disable it first to remove it from Claude Code.
The credentials are also in that file, readable only by its owner.
TermiNow connected from this app. This does not show that Claude Code in %1$s can reach the server: it may have a different network, proxy or certificates. No tool was called.

This server requires OAuth sign-in, which TermiNow does not support in this release, so it could not be tested.\n\nClaude Code can sign in itself: configure the server without credentials, then run /mcp in Claude Code and choose to authenticate.
Check the token or headers of the profile.
Updating the configuration and checking it with Claude Code…
The container %1$s is not installed anymore. TermiNow does not install it.
Claude Code was not found in %1$s.
This Claude Code (%1$s) does not support HTTP MCP servers. Update it first.
The project directory %1$s does not exist in %2$s.
TermiNow can not write %1$s in this environment.
The configuration changed since the preview. Nothing was written, configure again to see the change.
Claude Code did not answer in time.
You can set it up yourself with the manual setup commands.
This updates the entry that TermiNow wrote before.
The entry is already there as it should be. Nothing is written, Claude Code is only asked to confirm it.
The entry is not in the configuration anymore. The server is only marked as disabled.

An entry named %1$s is already there, and TermiNow did not write it or it was changed since:
%2$s

Replace it? A backup is made first.

The entry %1$s was not written by TermiNow or was changed since:
%2$s

Remove it anyway? A backup is made first.
The file is backed up next to it first, and written as a whole so it is never half written. All other settings stay as they are.

Claude Code reads the credentials of a server from its configuration, so they will be stored in %1$s as plain text, readable only by its owner (permissions 600). They are then not only in the encrypted store of TermiNow.

resources.string: Managing MCP servers is part of TermiNow Premium. Your saved servers are kept, and servers already added to Claude Code keep working there.
Endpoints come from the documentation of each provider, checked %1$s. TermiNow runs a tool only when you run it yourself and confirm its arguments.
Transport: remote, the documentation does not give the exact URL
TermiNow does not sign in with OAuth itself: its test shows Login required. Add the server to Claude Code and sign in there with /mcp.
The endpoint and sign-in are from the official documentation, checked %1$s.
From the official documentation, checked %1$s. Nothing is filled in that it does not give exactly.
TermiNow can not run or test local servers yet. Copy the command to add it to Claude Code in the environment that has its runtime, like your Ubuntu.
From the catalog: %1$s. Sign-in: %2$s. Review the fields before saving.
The command and each argument are passed as they are, never through a shell. Variable values are stored encrypted with a key in the Android keystore and are never shown again.
In TermiNow the command runs with the environment of the terminal. In a container it runs as the chosen user, with what is installed there.
No container is installed, so the command runs in TermiNow.
Starting the command. The first start can take a minute while it downloads its package.
From the last connection, %1$s. Connect to run them.
Connect to see the tools of this server.
The server has more tools than TermiNow shows.
Cancelled. TermiNow asked the server to stop the tool
Arguments, exactly as they are sent (saved secrets are hidden here)
The server runs the tool with the credentials of this server profile, and the tool may change data.
The server says that this tool only reads. It runs with the credentials of this server profile.
The server says that this tool can delete or overwrite data. Check the arguments before you run it.
An image (%1$s) that can not be shown
… %1$d more characters. Copy to get all of it.
TermiNow could not reach the server.
Check the internet connection and the URL, then reconnect.
The secure connection to the server failed.
The server needs a valid certificate. TermiNow never skips the check.
The server did not answer in time.
Try again. For a slow tool, raise its timeout.
The server needs an OAuth sign-in, which TermiNow can not do yet.
Use a token if the server offers one, or use the server from Claude Code and sign in with /mcp there.
Check the token or the header values: edit the server and enter them again.
The token may lack a permission that the server needs.
The server sent TermiNow to another URL.
If you trust the new URL, edit the server and enter it. TermiNow never follows a redirect with your credentials.
The server answered with an HTTP error.
Check the URL. If the server restarted or ended the session, reconnect.
The server did not answer like an MCP server.
Check that the URL is the MCP endpoint, or that the command starts an MCP server that speaks stdio.
The server speaks a protocol version that TermiNow does not support.
The server uses the old HTTP+SSE transport.
Use its Streamable HTTP endpoint, which often ends in /mcp.
The server answered with an error.
The details below are from the server.
Its last output is below. A missing package, API key or argument is a common cause.
The server command could not start.
Check the command, and that it is installed where it runs: in TermiNow, or in the container.
